observations.text: SP performed the turning rejoin after pitch out within the standards required for this block, with the IP directing the rejoin angle and the closure control throughout the maneuver. Visual on the formation leader was kept continuously and the velocity vector was never pointed at the leading A/C. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent control of the pursuit curve and of the airspeed in route position is expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP, following the formation leader's command, executed the turning rejoin and stabilized in route position with the rejoin angle held at 20 degrees and the airspeed 15 knots above the leader's, needing only the IP's verbal prompts on closure. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, but without the IP taking the A/C. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the turning rejoin in Fingertip after T/O, controlled the pursuit curve and stabilized in route position with a rejoin angle deviation of 15 degrees and an altitude 75 feet from No1 level. The errors were minor and were self-corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the turning rejoin after pitch out with smooth and solid control of the A/C, initially approaching the leading A/C at the same altitude and afterwards descending at the wing's level, holding the rejoin angle within 8 degrees and the airspeed in route position within 4 knots. Visual on the formation leader was kept continuously and no IP prompt was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the turning rejoin with exceptional accuracy, controlling Aspect Angle and Angle Off so that the rejoin angle deviation remained within 3 degrees, the airspeed in route position within 2 knots and the altitude within 15 feet of No1 level. The velocity vector was never pointed at the formation leader until his stabilization in route. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a late reduction of the pursuit curve at high Angle Off, did not control the closure on the leading A/C during the turning rejoin after pitch out, with the result of a rejoin angle deviation of about 28 degrees and an overtake that was stopped only when the IP took the A/C. The Overshoot was executed by the IP, because the SP did not inform the formation leader in time.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, pointed the velocity vector at the formation leader before his stabilization in route, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and executed part of the rejoin. At the moment of the IP's intervention the airspeed in route position was 25 knots above the leader's and the rejoin angle deviation exceeded 25 degrees.

SP executed the turning rejoin in Fingertip after T/O within the standards required for this block, holding the rejoin angle at the 20 degree limit and the airspeed in route position 15 knots above the leader's, with the errors recognized and corrected after the IP's verbal prompts. Visual on the formation leader was maintained throughout the maneuver. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the closure rate is expected to improve over the following rejoin repetitions.

SP, following the formation leader's command, executed the turning rejoin controlling Aspect Angle and Angle Off, with a rejoin angle deviation of 14 degrees and an altitude 70 feet from No1 level. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the turning rejoin after pitch out accurately and with speed, initially approaching the leading A/C at the same altitude and afterwards descending at the wing's level, holding the rejoin angle within 9 degrees and the altitude within 40 feet of No1 level. Control of the A/C was smooth and solid and no IP prompt was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the turning rejoin with exceptional precision, stabilizing in route position with the airspeed within 2 knots of the leader's and the altitude within 10 feet of No1 level. Continuous visual on the formation leader and correct management of the pursuit curve were demonstrated throughout the rejoin. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an excessive angle of bank applied late in the rejoin turn, did not establish the correct pursuit curve on the leading A/C, with the result of a rejoin angle deviation of about 30 degrees and closure that could not be stopped without the IP taking the A/C. The Overshoot was directed and partly executed by the IP.

SP, due to a failure to pass the required call at the briefed point, did not inform the formation leader that the Overshoot had become unavoidable, with the result that the Overshoot was initiated by the IP with the A/C 130 feet below No1 level. Visual on the formation leader was interrupted during the maneuver and was regained only on the IP's direction.

SP, due to a late power reduction on the closure leg, did not stabilize the airspeed in route position, with the result of an overtake of 15 knots and a rejoin angle held at the 20 degree limit. The condition was recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal prompts, without the IP taking the A/C.

SP, due to a failure to shed a secondary cockpit task when workload increased in the rejoin turn, did not keep continuous visual on the formation leader, with the result of a rejoin angle deviation of 20 degrees and an altitude 100 feet from No1 level. Visual and rejoin geometry were re-established only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delay.

SP executed the turning rejoin after pitch out within the desired standards for this block, with a rejoin angle deviation of 18 degrees and an airspeed in route position 13 knots above the leader's before stabilization. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention, and visual on the formation leader was kept continuously. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the pursuit curve and of the closure rate is expected to improve in the following sorties.

SP executed the turning rejoin in Fingertip after T/O accurately and with speed, holding the rejoin angle within 7 degrees, the airspeed in route position within 4 knots and the altitude within 30 feet of No1 level. The velocity vector was never pointed at the formation leader until his stabilization in route. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the turning rejoin with exceptional accuracy, controlling Aspect Angle, Angle Off and the pursuit curve so that the rejoin angle deviation did not exceed 3 degrees and the airspeed in route position stayed within 2 knots of the leader's. The A/C was flown in a smooth and solid manner throughout, with continuous visual on the formation leader. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect initial geometry that placed the A/C inside the leader's turn radius, did not establish a controllable pursuit curve on the turning rejoin, with the result of a rejoin angle deviation of about 30 degrees and an overtake of 25 knots in route position. The IP took the A/C and executed the Overshoot.

SP, due to a failure to make the knock-it-off call when the briefed rejoin parameters were exceeded, continued the rejoin with closure that could no longer be stopped, with the result that the A/C descended 140 feet below No1 level and the IP directed and executed the Overshoot. The formation leader was not informed that the Overshoot had become unavoidable.

SP, due to a delayed transition from the pursuit curve to the wing's level, did not descend at the wing's level after the initial approach at the same altitude, with the result of an altitude deviation of 100 feet from No1 level and a rejoin angle held at the 20 degree limit. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to degraded situational awareness after the leader's unplanned change of the rejoin direction, did not keep continuous visual on the formation leader during the turning rejoin, with the result of a rejoin angle deviation of 20 degrees and an airspeed in route position 15 knots above the leader's. Visual and rejoin geometry were re-established only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delay.

SP, due to a late power addition on the outside of the rejoin turn, did not hold the briefed closure on the leading A/C, with the result of an airspeed in route position 12 knots below the leader's and a rejoin angle deviation of 15 degrees. The error was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to complacency on a rejoin flown repeatedly without incident, did not execute the turning tactical rejoin according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, entering the leader's turn from a bearing outside the briefed cone before correcting to the prescribed line. The A/C was controlled smoothly and the error was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. Specific criteria are not applied on tactical rejoin.

SP executed the turning rejoin after pitch out accurately and with sufficiency, holding the rejoin angle within 10 degrees, the airspeed in route position within 5 knots and the altitude within 50 feet of No1 level, that is at the edge of the desired values. Control of the A/C was smooth and solid and visual on the formation leader was kept continuously. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a wider margin inside the desired parameters is expected in the following sorties.

SP executed the turning rejoin with exceptional accuracy, above the desired levels, holding the rejoin angle within 3 degrees, the airspeed in route position within 2 knots and the altitude within 15 feet of No1 level. The velocity vector was never pointed at the formation leader until his stabilization in route and the A/C was flown in a smooth and solid manner throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.
